Discuss at least two plausible causes and explain how your measurements distinguish them. Do not assume the provided observations prove one cause.
hold-summary

Summarize the following fictional experiment in five bullet points, preserving the important numbers and uncertainty. A team compared two storage layouts on the same server with 64 GB of memory and eight worker threads. The baseline stored 10 million records as separately allocated objects. The alternative stored fixed-width fields in contiguous arrays and variable-length strings in a separate arena. They warmed the filesystem cache, then ran seven repetitions of a scan that selected records with an integer field above a threshold. The baseline median was 840 ms and the alternative median was 390 ms. The slowest alternative run was 510 ms. A point-lookup workload improved only from 12 to 11 ms. Updating one percent of records became slower, rising from 140 to 190 ms. Memory use fell from 9.2 to 6.4 GB. They did not measure cold-cache scans, larger-than-memory data, or concurrent updates. They suspect locality explains much of the scan improvement, but did not collect hardware counters. State which conclusions are supported and which follow-up measurement is most useful.
